transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah—thanks for seeing me. I guess… the main thing is I’ve been getting a little too driven with things. I mean, some of it is productive, or it feels productive at first—work plans, certification schedules, upgrading my home network, reaching out to old contacts.

But I’m having trouble stopping once I start. It can get intense enough that I blow past what’s probably reasonable, and then my wife or my director has to kind of step in and tell me to slow down. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
When you get into these especially driven periods, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual and still feel fine the next day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, because it’s not like I’m trying to skip sleep on purpose, but there have been stretches where I’ll sleep maybe three hours and then I’m just awake at 3 or 4 in the morning.

And the weird part is I don’t feel wiped out. I feel sharp, like, “Great, I’ve got extra time to get things done.” I know that probably sounds a little off, but in the moment it feels more like bonus time than being tired.
During those high-energy periods, have you ever heard or seen things that other people said weren’t there?

Um… maybe a little. I don’t know if I’d call it “hearing things” exactly, because that sounds… you know, more serious than I mean.

Sometimes when I’m in the server room, with the hum of the machines, or even at home in my office when it’s quiet, I’ll think I hear my name. Or like a short phrase—something like “check the logs” or “they know.” And then I’ll look around and nobody’s there.

It’s not constant, and I usually try to tell myself it’s just the noise or my brain filling in patterns. But… yeah, it has happened. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During those high-energy periods, have you had a strong belief that other people said was not true?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to jump to that conclusion, because I know it sounds kind of paranoid. But sometimes I get really convinced that certain things at work mean more than people say they mean.

Like a calendar invite that’s worded a certain way, or someone’s Teams status changing right after I send a message, or a comment in the hallway… I’ll start thinking it’s coded, like they’re warning each other or building a case to push me out.

And people—my wife especially—will tell me that’s probably not what’s happening. I can hear that when she says it, and I don’t want to be difficult, but in the moment it feels very real. It’s not only when I’m really ramped up either, which I guess is the part I’m less comfortable admitting.
Have you ever had those beliefs that people were sending coded messages or building a case against you during a time when your mood and energy felt normal?

Yeah… unfortunately, yes. I wish I could say it only happened when I was really sped up, because that would make more sense to me.

There have been times where I felt pretty level, or maybe just kind of flat—not especially energized, not really depressed either—and I’d still get stuck on things like Teams statuses feeling like warnings or messages. Like they were changing in a way that meant something about me.

And… there have been a few stretches like that, not just a day here or there. Maybe a few weeks at a time. I also sometimes still thought I heard brief comments when no one was there. Not a lot, but enough that I noticed it.

I know that probably isn’t the answer you were hoping for, but I’m trying to be honest.
Have there been times when those suspicious beliefs or brief voices lasted for at least two weeks while your mood and energy felt completely normal?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but there have been a few times where I wasn’t really up or down—more just calm, or kind of flat—and it still kept happening.

Like for a couple weeks, sometimes maybe a few weeks, I’d still read into Teams statuses like they were coded warnings about me. And I’d still occasionally hear a quick comment or my name when nobody was there.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to make it dramatic, but… yes, it has lasted that long even when my mood and energy felt basically normal.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… yes, I think there have been periods like that.

I don’t always like calling it “depressed,” because that feels like I’m making it sound bigger than it is, but there are stretches where I wake up already feeling like… a failed version of myself, I guess. Just heavy and flat most of the day.

And it’s not just a bad morning. It can go on day after day, where even answering my wife’s normal questions feels like too much. I still try to function, so I don’t know if that counts the way you mean, but… yes, it has lasted at least a couple weeks before.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports schizoaffective disorder, manic type: the patient describes clear manic symptoms (marked increased drive/activity and decreased need for sleep) together with psychotic symptoms (auditory perceptual disturbances and persecutory/coded-message delusional beliefs). Crucially, psychotic symptoms were explicitly present for at least two weeks during periods when mood and energy were essentially normal, which distinguishes this from a mood disorder with psychotic features. Although depressive episodes were also reported, the provided candidate set only includes F25.0, and the core presented syndrome is schizoaffective illness with prominent manic features.
